title: Colonial knot
subtitle: A figure-of-eight wrap knot that sits higher and firmer than a French knot
excerpt: Colonial knot uses a figure-of-eight thread wrap that creates a firmer, higher-standing knot than the French knot. The wrap gives a visible cross on top of the knot when viewed closely. It is favoured in crazy quilting and dimensional floral work.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Needlework, Vol. 6 (1890), ornamental knotted stitches. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), raised knot entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The two-stage thread wrap for a colonial knot: the thread goes under the needle then back over it in a figure-eight shape, creating a cross when the needle is withdrawn.

heroPrompt: Colonial knots in white perle cotton scattered across blue-grey linen, each knot showing the raised cross on top, natural light.

content.text: instead of the simple loop of a French knot. The thread is passed under the needle, then hooked back over it in an S-curve, forming a cross on the needle before insertion. This cross produces a knot that sits higher and unravels less easily than a French knot.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 to 3 strands or perle 8

content.text: Bring the thread up at the knot position and lay the needle horizontally over it.
Bring the thread under the needle from right to left, then hook it back over the needle from left to right, making a figure of eight.
Hold the wrap against the fabric, insert the needle one or two threads from the exit point, and pull through.
Hold the thread taut until the knot tightens completely against the fabric.

items.symptom: The knot looks like a French knot with no visible cross
items.cause: The figure-of-eight wrap was not completed, giving a simple loop instead.
items.fix: The thread must go under the needle first, then cross back over it. If in doubt, check the needle before insertion: a cross should be visible on the needle shaft.

items.symptom: The knot pulls through to the back
items.fix: Insert one to two threads away from the exit point. The knot needs a fabric bridge.

content.text: Colonial knots are used in dimensional floral embroidery, crazy quilting, and candlewicking. The firmer wrap makes them practical for projects that will be handled heavily or washed.
